scope: third-pass inference audit over the post-#239/#241 racer-native seams, recovered Widescreen scene policy, closed gameplay-authored progression acceptance, and the latest native Restart Race negative

findings.title: Racer replacement identity and screen placement are independent presentation coordinates

result.identity_source: authoritative WRAM composition/frame state through the native read-only racer guest snapshot and replacement selector
result.placement_source: live SNES PPU OAM/high-OAM/OBSEL through the native placement decoder
result.consequence: replacement asset selection can be cached/keyed by semantic racer presentation identity while position, size and H/V orientation are applied from live OAM each frame; screen coordinates do not belong in the semantic asset key

findings.falsifier: A retained runtime state in the same racer family where the same semantic presentation tuple requires a different replacement raster before OAM/OBSEL transforms are applied.
findings.next_action: Keep replacement lookup and placement transform as separate interfaces in the first pixel-substitution hook.

findings.title: The first HD racer replacement seam can remain zero-authority over guest state

result.implication: A draw-frame replacement prototype does not need to patch WRAM, animation timing, OAM, or simulation to choose and position a remastered racer.

findings.falsifier: A required replacement decision that cannot be derived from the retained semantic WRAM tuple plus live PPU presentation state without modifying authoritative state.
findings.next_action: Make Original fallback the only failure mode for unknown/unregistered presentation tuples.

findings.title: Widescreen policy is domain-specific and viewport-local, not one global widen switch

result.implication: The implementation should widen presentation per viewport while preserving stock activation/simulation boundaries; split-screen does not justify widening authoritative world liveness.

findings.falsifier: An event-relative fixture proving that correct widened presentation requires earlier authoritative object activation or changed race simulation.
findings.next_action: Use the existing VS-mode discriminator to decide whether VS shares ordinary-2P presentation policy, without changing the ownership model.

findings.title: Modern profile state should coordinate guest SRAM, not absorb progression semantics

result.guest_owned: 8 KiB SRAM medal/tier/checksum state with gameplay-authored save/reload acceptance
result.host_owned: profile identity and modern administrative settings
result.implication: Future autosave/resume metadata should reference or snapshot guest-owned SRAM as an opaque authoritative payload; medal/tier fields should not be duplicated into HostProductState as a second source of truth.

findings.falsifier: A concrete modern feature that cannot preserve stock progression authority while storing only host metadata plus guest SRAM/save artifacts.
findings.next_action: Design autosave catalog metadata around guest save provenance/versioning rather than a parallel medal database.

findings.title: Immediate whole-machine snapshot equality is insufficient to certify Restart Race

result.implication: A restart acceptance must prove forward deterministic replay across APU as well as immediate serialized-state equality; the current restart implementation is not accepted.

findings.falsifier: A corrected lifecycle/state implementation that restores and replays the same accepted window with all compared partitions equal.
findings.next_action: Audit which APU timing/runtime state is outside the restored snapshot or is advanced asymmetrically around restore; keep Restart Race disabled until replay equality closes.

findings.title: The accepted stock-helper Widescreen mechanism has a natural one-column (+8 px) capacity boundary

latest_native_hook_observation.caveat: native-hook PR #228 remains unmerged because 11 of 617 +8 PREP events failed the strict immediate-adjacency predicate

result.implication: +16/+24 cannot be obtained merely by consuming more of the same single spare stock lane at one preparation boundary; generalization needs additional queue/storage capacity or a different scheduling strategy.

findings.falsifier: A stock-compatible scheduling construction that prepares two or more additional horizontal columns at the same required boundary without expanding lane capacity and while preserving protected state.
findings.next_action: Resolve the 11 non-adjacent +8 events before promoting the native hook; treat +16/+24 as an explicit capacity-extension problem rather than a parameter tweak.

new_runtime_work_admission: HD racer pixel substitution can proceed without new guest-state mutation research; identity and placement inputs are already separated.
Restart Race needs a targeted APU restore/replay discriminator, not broader snapshot experimentation.
Widescreen beyond +8 should investigate queue/lane capacity only after the +8 adjacency exceptions are explained.
Modern autosave/profile work should preserve guest SRAM as the authoritative progression substrate.
audit_conclusions.canonical_status_note: IA3-R01 and IA3-W02 preserve the original third-pass evidence, with their 2026-10-03 resolutions recorded in subsequent_disposition.
current_runtime_admission: HD racer pixel substitution can proceed on the read-only semantic-identity/live-placement seam.
Restart Race runtime restore/replay semantics are accepted; remaining work is product/UI integration.
+8 native Widescreen preparation is accepted and merged; +16/+24 require a deliberate larger presentation-capacity seam.
Modern autosave/profile work should preserve guest SRAM as the authoritative progression substrate.

IA3-R01.root_cause: SNESRecomp rollback residue restored APU pacing counters but omitted the extended RtlApuFrameClock; residue v7 now captures/restores it
IA3-R01.durable_rule: Immediate snapshot equality is insufficient; Restart Race acceptance requires deterministic forward replay.

IA3-W02.root_cause: The 11 apparent adjacency failures came from comparing the full edge word; low five bits are the 32-column VRAM-ring coordinate and upper bits may change at resource/segment boundaries.
IA3-W02.remaining_boundary: +16/+24 still require more than the one spare secondary horizontal lane and remain a presentation-capacity extension problem.
